subject: Material selection for reliable manufacture
hook: What happens to your cutting list after you hit send.
ig:
What happens to your cutting list after you hit send? Six stages, start to finish.

For trade customers, the frustrating part of outsourcing is usually not knowing where your job is. So here's how a typical order runs through our Hanley workshop:

1. List check — spec questions answered before cutting, not after
2. Priced cutting list — approved by you first
3. Cut on the sliding table panel saw
4. Edged and, if ordered, drilled
5. Assembled, if you want carcasses ready to fit
6. Wrapped for collection, or delivery quoted per job

Stage 1 is where most time is saved. A clear list with decor codes, thickness and edging per edge goes straight through.

Swipe through, then DM us 'TRADE' to send your next cutting list.
fb:
Sending work out for cutting and edging is only worth it if you know what's happening to it.

This carousel walks through a typical trade order in our Hanley workshop: list check, priced cutting list, cutting, edging and drilling, optional assembly, then collection or delivery.

The list check is where most time is saved: exact decor codes, board thickness and edging marked per edge mean the job goes straight onto the saw.

Cut only or fully assembled, trade or domestic — ask us for a priced cutting list.

on_asset: F1: List check — We read through sizes, sheet size, decor, thickness, grain and edging before anything is cut, and come back with questions early. | F2: Priced and confirmed — You get a priced cutting list to approve, so you know the cost before work starts. | F3: Cut — Sheets cut to size on our sliding table panel saw in Hanley. | F4: Edged and drilled — ABS edging to your spec, then hinge cups, shelf-pin rows or dowel holes on the boring machine if ordered. | F5: Assembled (optional) — Carcasses, drawer units or tall units built up if you'd rather fit than assemble. | F6: Ready — Wrapped for workshop collection, or delivery quoted per job.
